nahhas-meani:170-170.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِٱلْكِتَابِ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿يُمَسِّكُونَ بِٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ is: they follow what is in it and judge by it.
﴿إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ﴾ that is, whoever among them reformed, believed and did not stubbornly resist.

nahhas-meani:171-171.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذ نَتَقْنَا ٱلْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ﴾.
One says: نَتَقْتُ الشَّيءَ، أنْتُقُه، نَتْقاً، ونُتُوقاً (I shook the thing loose), when you shake it and hurl it, or cut it off; and from this comes امرأةٌ ناتِقٌ, that is, a woman who bears many children, as though she throws out children.
And one says: نَتَقْتُ السِّقَاءَ, when you shake the skin-bag to bring out the butter that is in it.
Qatāda said: The mountain was raised over their heads, and Moses ﷺ said to them: If you accept what is in the Book [well and good]; otherwise it will fall upon you.
And the meaning of ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ is: with earnestness.

nahhas-meani:172-172.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾.
The best of what has been said about this is what the reports from the Prophet ﷺ have transmitted in abundance: "Allah, Mighty and Glorious, wiped the back of Adam and brought out from it his offspring, like tiny ants (al-dharr), and took the covenant from them." So it is as though He made them understand what He, Mighty and Glorious, intended, just as the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ﴾.
And in the ḥadīth: "Every child is born upon the fiṭra (the original disposition)."
That is, upon the beginning of his affair, when He took the covenant from them.
"Abū Jaʿfar related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Muqriʾ al-Baghdādī related to us in al-Ramla, saying: ʿAbbās al-Dūrī related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī related to us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū l-ʿĀliya, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, concerning this verse: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿المُبْطِلُون﴾. He said: He gathered them and made them into pairs, then He shaped them, then He made them speak, and said: ﴿أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدْنَآ﴾ — that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord besides You and no god besides You. He said: Then I shall send My messengers to you and send down My Books upon you, so do not deny My messengers, and believe My threat; and I shall take vengeance on whoever associates partners with Me and does not believe in Me. So He took their pledge and their covenant." And he mentioned the ḥadīth.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We shall mention the ḥadīth of ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ on the meaning of this verse in the I'rab [book], and elsewhere, if Allah wills.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ﴾.
This is the complete stop (al-tamām), according to the reading of those who read ﴿أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾ with tāʾ.
Abū Ḥātim said: That is our position, because of His saying ﴿أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾? He is addressing them, so He said, by way of address: ﴿أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾, that is, so that you would not say.
And Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others read ﴿أنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ with yāʾ, and the meaning on this reading is: and He made them bear witness over themselves out of aversion to their saying.

nahhas-meani:175-175.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيۤ آتَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا فَٱنْسَلَخَ مِنْهَا﴾.
Shuʿba narrated, from Manṣūr, from Abū l-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: He is "Balʿām".
Ibn Abī Jurayj narrated, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is "Balʿām ibn Bāʿir", of the Children of Israel.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "He had with him the Greatest Name of Allah, so they asked him to invoke Allah against Moses, peace be upon him, and his companions. He said: Give me time — and he would not invoke against anyone until he saw that in his sleep. So he spent the night and was forbidden in his sleep. Then they came back to him — Moses ﷺ had come upon them with eighty thousand, beyond the Euphrates — and when they asked him to invoke against him after he had been forbidden, he said to them: Send the women out to his companions so that they are tempted, and you will be given victory over them. So he slipped out of what he had been in; and he had been commanded in his sleep to invoke in his favour."
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah have mercy on them both, said: "He is your fellow, Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt."
And ʿIkrima said: He is whoever was [of] the Jews and the Christians whose Islam was not sound.
He means that they are the hypocrites of the People of the Book.
And Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿فَٱنْسَلَخَ مِنْهَا﴾: It is the knowledge that was stripped from him.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ﴾.
One says أتْبَعَهُ when he caught up with him, and تَبِعَهُ when he went in his tracks; this is the good [usage].
And it has been said: They are two dialectal forms.

nahhas-meani:176-176.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, We would have lifted him away from it [Translator's note: the Arabic has «لرفعناه عنه», "lifted it from him"]; and its meaning is: We would have protected him from what he did.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, he settled; and the implied sense (al-taqdīr) is: to the comforts of the earth and its pleasures.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْكَلْبِ إِن تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, if you charge at it with your mount or on foot it pants, or if you leave it, it pants; and likewise is the one who reads the Book and does not act on what is in it.
And someone other than Mujāhid said: This is the worst of similitudes, in that his whim has overcome him until he no longer has power to harm or benefit himself — [likened] to a dog that is always panting, whether it is charged at or not charged at; it has no power to stop panting.

nahhas-meani:179-179.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيراً مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْسِ﴾.
[That is, We created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind.
One says: ذَرَأَ اللهُ خلقه يَذْرَؤُهُم ذَرْءاً] that is, He created them.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ كَٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾ — He described them as being in the rank of that which does not reason.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ﴾.
Because cattle, when they see what harms them, avoid it, or most of it, and they do not disbelieve out of stubborn resistance.

nahhas-meani:180-180.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَللَّهِ ٱلأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ فَٱدْعُوهُ بِهَا﴾.
Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Allah has ninety-nine names, a hundred less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise."
And one of the philologists said: According to this, it is obligatory that Allah, Mighty and Glorious, be invoked only by what He has described Himself with; so one says: يَا جَوادُ (O Bountiful), and one does not say: يا سَخِيُّ (O Generous).
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِيۤ أَسْمَآئِهِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: They derived al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and al-Lāt from Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ilḥād in the language is deviating and inclining; and from it comes laḥd al-qabr (the side-niche of the grave), because it is not in the middle, rather it inclines to its side.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Kisāʾī distinguished between ألْحَدَ and لَحَدَ, saying: ألحد means to turn away from the right course, and لَحَدَ means to lean towards a thing.
And on this basis he read in [Sūrat] al-Naḥl ﴿يَلْحَدُونَ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, in the sense of leaning.

nahhas-meani:182-182.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِّنْ حَيْثُ لاَ يَعْلَمُون﴾.
One says: استدرج فلانٌ فلاناً (so-and-so drew so-and-so on step by step), when he does something intending to cast him into ruin.
And istidrāj is only stage after stage; and from it comes فلانٌ يُدْرِجُ فلاناً, and from it أدْرجتُ الثَّوب (I folded the garment).

nahhas-meani:183-183.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ﴾.
The meaning of "أُمْلِي" is: I defer; and al-malāwa is a stretch of time — it is said with ḍamma and with kasra — and from it comes: تَمِلَّ حَبيبك (enjoy your beloved for a long while). And al-matīn is: the strong.

nahhas-meani:185-185.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُواْ فِي مَلَكُوتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Sufyān said: He means the creation of the heavens and the earth.

nahhas-meani:187-187.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, when is its coming to pass?
And someone else said: One says رسى الشيءُ، يرسو، رُسُوًّا when it is firmly fixed, and أرْسَيْتُهُ: I fixed it firmly.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي﴾.
That is, none knows when it will come to pass except Allah.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿لاَ يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ﴾.
One says: جَلَّى ليَ فلانٌ الخَبَر, when he disclosed the news and made it clear.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿ثَقُلَتْ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ لاَ تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلاَّ بَغْتَةً﴾.
That is, knowledge of it is hidden, and when a thing is hidden it is heavy.
And it has been said: That is, the question about it is heavy, that is, it is grave.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿لاَ تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلاَّ بَغْتَةً﴾.
That is, suddenly.
* And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: We are your kinsmen, so tell us in secret when the Hour is. So Allah, Mighty and Glorious, sent down ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْهَا﴾, that is, solicitous towards them.
And the meaning on this view involves fronting and postponement (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr), that is: they ask you about it as though you were solicitous towards them, that is, glad at their asking.
And this is the meaning of the statement of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that is, they ask you as though you were solicitous towards them.

nahhas-meani:188-188.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَلَوْ كُنتُ أَعْلَمُ ٱلْغَيْبَ لاَسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: If I knew the year of famine and drought, I would have prepared for it what would suffice me.
And it has been said: If I knew when I would die, I would have done much worship; so "good" (al-khayr) here is worship.
And it has been said: The Prophet ﷺ used to be asked about what was in people's hearts and what they kept secret, so he said: ﴿وَلَوْ كُنتُ أَعْلَمُ ٱلْغَيْبَ﴾, that is, what they keep secret and what will befall you, so that you might beware of its harm, it would be more fitting that you respond to me in what I call you to; ﴿لاَسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾, that is, of your responding to what I call you to; ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ ٱلسُّوۤءُ﴾ from you, by denial or enmity, since I would be [regarded] among you as such.
And what indicates this answer is ﴿إِنْ أَنَاْ إِلاَّ نَذِيرٌ﴾, that is, I do not know of the Unseen except what Allah has taught me.
And it has been said: ﴿وَلَوْ كُنتُ أَعْلَمُ ٱلْغَيْبَ﴾, that is, the Books of Allah.
And al-Ḥasan said: ﴿لاَسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾: of revelation.

nahhas-meani:189-189.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾.
He means Adam ﷺ; ﴿وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ He means Eve; ﴿فَلَماَّ تَغَشَّاهَا﴾ is a kināya (euphemism) for intercourse; ﴿حَمَلَتْ حَمْلاً خَفِيفاً فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, she continued with it; and the meaning is that she passed [her time] with it and came and went without it weighing her down.
And Ibn Yaʿmar read ﴿فَمَرَتْ بِهِ﴾, without doubling, that is, she was in doubt about the pregnancy.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him: she continued with it.
Abū Ḥātim said: That is, the pregnancy continued with her, and he inverted the expression, as one says: I put the boot into my foot.
﴿فَلَمَّآ أَثْقَلَتْ﴾ that is, her pregnancy became evident; ﴿دَّعَوَا ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُمَا لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنَا صَالِحاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, a boy.
And Abū l-Bakhtarī said: They feared it would be an animal.

nahhas-meani:190-190.t:
Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آتَاهُمَا صَالِحاً جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَآءَ فِيمَآ آتَاهُمَا﴾.
Khuṣayf narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Iblīs came to them and said: I am the one who got you both out of the Garden; so if you obey me [well and good], otherwise I will put two horns on it so that it splits your belly, or I will bring it out dead. And it was decreed that it should come out dead. Then she conceived another pregnancy and he said the like of that to them [and it was decreed that it should come out dead; then she conceived another pregnancy and he said the like of that to them]. Then Eve said to him: In what do you want me to obey you? He said: Name him "ʿAbd al-Ḥārith". So she named him so, and Allah, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَآءَ فِيمَآ آتَاهُمَا﴾.
Someone else said: He means in the naming specifically; and the name of "Iblīs" was al-Ḥārith.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَتَعَالَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
That is, above what the unbelievers associate [with Him]; and what indicates this is ﴿أيُشْرِكُونَ مَا لاَ يَخْلُقُ شَيْئاً﴾? He means the idols.
And it is narrated from ʿIkrima that he said: Adam and Eve alone are not singled out by this; and the implied sense on this view is: the whole of the species, that is, He created each one of you ﴿مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا﴾, that is, from its kind, ﴿زَوْجَهَا فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاهَا﴾ referring to the whole species; and likewise ﴿دَعَوَا﴾ is meant to refer to the two unbelieving kinds; then ﴿فَتَعَالَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ is construed according to the meaning of all of them. And this is more fitting — and Allah knows best — than that the like of this be attributed to the prophets, peace be upon them.
And some of the people of speculative reasoning (ahl al-naẓar) said: Someone other than "Adam and Eve" is meant by it, and they were only mentioned because they are the origin of mankind.

nahhas-meani:194-194.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾.
That is, Allah, Mighty and Glorious, destroys them as He destroys you.
And it is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he read: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾ [Translator's note: the variant intended is presumably «إنِ الذين… عباداً أمثالَكم» with negating إنْ; the source text prints the standard reading here], and "إنْ" here has the meaning of "ما" (not), and the meaning is: those whom you call upon besides Allah are not servants like you, that is, they are the idols. And the first reading is more widespread and better known, and the main body [of the muṣḥaf/reciters] (al-sawād) is upon it.

nahhas-meani:196-196.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ وَلِيِّـيَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾.
Al-Akhfash said: And it has been read ﴿إنَّ وَلِيَّ اللهِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الكِتَابَ﴾, meaning Gabriel ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is the reading of ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī; and the first reading is more fitting, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:198-198.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِن تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ لاَ يَسْمَعُواْ وَتَرَاهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ لاَ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
He means the idols.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says: داري تنظر إلى دار فلان (my house "looks at" so-and-so's house), when it is near to it.

nahhas-meani:199-199.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَاهِلِينَ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ said: Al-ʿafw is: the surplus.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language: whatever was surplus and was not by strain.
Abū Jaʿfar related to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Ṣūfī related to us, saying: Dāwūd al-Ḍabbī informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khālid related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ﴾: He said: Take from their characters and their deeds without prying.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: This was before charity (ṣadaqa) was made obligatory, and zakāt has abrogated it.
And Wahb ibn Kaysān said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, say: ﴿خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ﴾: By Allah, he was commanded only that it be taken from people's characters; and by Allah, I shall take it from them as long as I keep company with them.
* Then He, Mighty and Glorious, said: ﴿وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ﴾.
And al-ʿurf is: al-maʿrūf (what is recognised as right).

nahhas-meani:200-200.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِماَّ يَنَزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾.
Al-nazgh is: the slightest movement.

nahhas-meani:201-201.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَواْ إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِّنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Al-ṭayf is: anger.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Al-ṭayf is: a touch (of madness) (al-lamam), and al-ṭāʾif is everything that circles around a person.
And Abū ʿAmr said: Al-ṭayf is: whispering (al-waswasa); and its real sense in the language is from طافَ يَطِيفُ: when something is imagined in the heart or seen in sleep; and it is ṭāʾif, and ṭayf has the same meaning.

nahhas-meani:202-202.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي ٱلْغَيِّ﴾.
That is, they increase them.

nahhas-meani:203-203.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذَا لَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بِآيَةٍ قَالُواْ لَوْلاَ ٱجْتَبَيْتَهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, [why have you not] brought it of your own accord?
And so it is in the language; one says: اجتبيتُ الشيءَ، وارتجلتُه، واخترعتُه، واختلقتُه, when you bring it of your own accord.

nahhas-meani:204-204.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ ٱلْقُرْآنُ فَٱسْتَمِعُواْ لَهُ وَأَنصِتُواْ﴾.
This is general in wording with a specific intent.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn Shihāb and al-Ḥasan said: This is in the prayer.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: This is in the prayer and the sermon (khuṭba).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting, because in the sermon silence is obligatory whether the Qurʾān is recited or not recited.
And the proof of its correctness is what Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī narrated, from Abū ʿIyāḍ, from Abū Hurayra, who said: They used to talk in the prayer, so Allah, Mighty and Glorious, sent down ﴿وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ ٱلْقُرْآنُ﴾ to its end.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And there has been no disagreement about the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾, that it concerns supplication.
And some of them said, concerning His saying, Mighty and Glorious, ﴿فَٱسْتَمِعُواْ لَهُ وَأَنصِتُواْ﴾: This was specifically for the Messenger of Allah, so that his Companions would retain it from him ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:205-205.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Glorious: ﴿وَدُونَ ٱلْجَهْرِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾.
Al-āṣāl are: the evenings; the singular is uṣul, and the singular of uṣul is aṣīl.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿الۤمۤصۤ﴾
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have explained the meaning of the openings of the sūras at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara. Whoever said the meaning of ﴿الم﴾ is "I am Allah, I know best" said the meaning of ﴿الۤمۤصۤ﴾ is "I am Allah, I make clear (afṣilu)".
This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾
The meaning is: this is a Book sent down to you.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: الحَرَج means doubt.
And the meaning according to this view is: so do not [you all] doubt it, because addressing the Prophet ﷺ is addressing his community.
And الحرج in the language is narrowness; it may be that [doubt] was called narrowness because the one who doubts does not know the reality of the thing, so his breast becomes constricted by it.
And it is possible that the meaning is: so let there be no constriction in your breast about conveying it, because it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I fear that they will smash my head."
And in the passage there is a fronting and a postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); the meaning is: a Book sent down to you that you may warn by it, and a reminder for the believers, so let there be no constriction in your breast from it.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
It is said: It is the Qurʾān and the Sunna, because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا آتَاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فخُذُوهُ، ومَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ قَلِيلاً مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾.
That is, do not take as an ally anyone who has turned away from the religion of truth; and everyone who is content with a doctrine, the people of that doctrine are his allies.
And it is reported from Mālik ibn Dīnār, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read ﴿ولا تبتغوا من دونه أولياء﴾, that is: do not seek.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا فَجَآءَهَا بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتاً أَوْ هُمْ قَآئِلُونَ﴾.
The meaning is: the punishment came to them unawares, by night while they were asleep, or at midday while they were taking their midday rest.
And the meaning of (أو) here is variation — once like this and once like that — and it is equivalent to the (أوْ) that expresses permission in a command.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَا كَانَ دَعْوَاهُمْ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَآ﴾.
الدعوى here is equivalent to الدعاء (supplication, calling). And الدعوى can be equivalent to الإِدِّعَاء (claim), and can be equivalent to الدُّعاء; and the grammarians permitted: "اللَّهُمَّ اشركْنَا في صَالِح دَعْوَى منْ دَعَاكَ" (O Allah, include us in the righteous supplication of whoever has called upon You).
And the meaning is: at the time of destruction they arrived at nothing but the admission that they had been wrongdoers.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
This is a questioning of rebuke and of making [them] confess.
As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ وَلاَ جَانٌّ﴾, its meaning is that he will not be asked a question seeking information. And Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْحَقُّ فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ ﴾.
ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: "On the Day of Resurrection the huge, tall man, the great eater and great drinker, will be brought, and he will not weigh a gnat's wing."
ʿAmr ibn Dīnār said: The Balance has two pans.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, We gave you possession.
﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ﴾.
That is, that by which you live.
And it is possible that the meaning is: that by which you attain a livelihood.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُواْ لأَدَمَ﴾.
There are several views on this verse:
Al-Akhfash said — and it is one of Quṭrub's two views — (ثمَّ) here is in the sense of the wāw.
This view is mistaken according to the school of the analytical grammarians (ahl al-naẓar); it is not permissible for (ثُمَّ) to be in the sense of the wāw, because their meanings differ.
And it is said: (ثُمَّ) is for [sequence in] reporting.
And it is said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ means in the loins of Ādam ﷺ, ﴿ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ﴾ means in the wombs; this is authentically reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ means the son of Ādam; He, Majestic and Mighty is He, knew that He would create his offspring, so it is as though He had [already] created [them].
And Mujāhid said — Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abī Najīḥ reported it from him: the meaning of ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ﴾ is in the loins of Ādam.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is the best of the views. Mujāhid holds that He created them in the loins of Ādam, then shaped them when He took the covenant from them, and then the prostration to Ādam came afterwards.
And this is strengthened by ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَاتِهِمْ﴾.
And the ḥadīth: "that He brought them out like tiny ants (al-dharr) and took the covenant from them."
Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning is: We created Ādam from dust, then We shaped him. He said: and this is indicated by ﴿خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾; so the implied construction (taqdīr) is: We created your origin.
And it is said: The meaning is: We created you as sperm-drops, then We shaped you.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَسَجَدُوۤاْ إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّاجِدِينَ﴾.
It is said: He excepted Iblīs from the angels though he was not one of them, because he was commanded to prostrate along with them; He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ ألاَّ تَسْجُدَ إذْ أَمَرْتُكَ﴾?
And it is said: He was one of them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have treated this exhaustively in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ﴾.
This is a question of rebuke and of making [him] confess, because He, Majestic and Mighty is He, already knew that.
And (لا) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, as [the poet] said:
فَمَا ألومُ البِيضَ أنْ لاَ تَسْخَرَا * لَمَّا رَأَيْنَ الشَّمْطَ القَفَنْدَرَا
(I do not blame the fair women for mocking when they saw the ugly grey-haired one.)
So he gave an answer to something other than what he was asked, saying: ﴿أَنَاْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ﴾, and did not say: such-and-such prevented me. It is rather the answer of one who has been asked: Which of you two is better? But it is construed according to the sense, as though he said: my superiority over him prevented me.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ أَنظِرْنِي إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾.
That is, grant me respite. He was not granted this exactly; rather he was granted respite until the Day of the Known Time.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِي لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾.
It is said: Its meaning is: because You have led me astray.
And it is said: Its meaning is: You have disappointed me (خيَّبْتَنِ).
And it is said: that is, because You called me to something on account of which I went astray. And Allah knows best what is meant.
Mujāhid said: The meaning of ﴿لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ is: I will surely lie in wait for them upon the truth.
And الصراط in the language is the road, and the meaning is: upon Your path; then (علَى) was omitted and the verb became transitive [Translator's note: directly — accusative by removal of the preposition].

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾.
Sufyān reported from Manṣūr from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, who said: ﴿مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: from their worldly life; ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾: from their Hereafter; ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: meaning their good deeds; ﴿وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾: meaning their evil deeds.
This is a good view, and its explanation is that the meaning of ﴿وَلآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ is: from their worldly life, so that they deny the signs in it and the reports of past nations;
﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾: from their Hereafter, so that they deny it;
﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: from their good deeds and the matters of their religion.
And this is indicated by His saying the Exalted: ﴿إنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ اليَمِينِ﴾.
﴿وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾ means their evil deeds, that is, they follow desires, because he makes them seem fair to them.
And it is said: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: from their Hereafter.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾.
As for His saying the Exalted ﴿مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, he says: I will make them doubt their Hereafter; ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾: I will make them desire their worldly life; ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: I will confuse for them the matter of their religion; ﴿وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾: I will make sins attractive to them; ﴿وَلاَ تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرِينَ﴾: he says: affirming [Allah's] oneness.
And with this same chain (isnād): ﴿مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ means from this world, ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ from the Hereafter, ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ from the side of their good deeds, ﴿وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾ from the side of their evil deeds.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That view is not impossible, because the Hereafter has not yet come, so it is before us; and it comes after our death, so from this angle it is said: it is behind us.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ is: he makes them fear for what they leave behind and for those they leave after them.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾ is: from every direction from which they act, and it is a figurative representation (tamthīl), because most activity is done with the two hands; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ﴾.
And Mujāhid said: ﴿مِّن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ، وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: from the good deeds; ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ، وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ﴾: from the evil deeds.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُوماً مَّدْحُوراً﴾.
One says: ذأمته, ذِمْتُه and ذَمَمْتُه with one meaning (I disparaged him).
And al-Aʿmash read: ﴿مَذُوماً﴾, and the meaning is the same, except that he lightened the hamza.
And Mujāhid said: المذؤمُ means the banished. And the two meanings are close.
And المدحور: the one driven away and removed far off; one says: "اللهمَّ ادْحَرْ عَنَّا الشَّيْطَانَ" (O Allah, drive Satan away from us).

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبَا هَـٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ ﴾.
It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was the ear of grain (al-sunbula).

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُورِيَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَاتِهِمَا﴾.
That is, to expose to them what had been concealed from them of their private parts; and from this: تواريت من فلانٍ (I hid myself from so-and-so).
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr read ﴿مَا أُوْرِيَ عَنْهُمَا﴾.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَالِدِينَ﴾.
Most people read it with fatḥa on the lām [مَلَكَيْنِ, "two angels"]. And the one who argued for kasra on the lām said that His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿وَمُلْكٍ لاَ يَبْلَى﴾ points to the reading "مَلِكَيْنِ" ("two kings"), because مُلْك (kingship) comes from مَلِك (king).
And Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ rejected kasra on the lām, and said: There was no king before Ādam ﷺ, such that they could become two kings.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّي لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّاصِحِينَ﴾.
He swore to them; [the form فاعَلَ here being of one party only,] like طارقتُ النَّعلَ (I double-soled the sandal).
And it is said: They both swore that they would not accept from him unless he swore, so he swore to them.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَدَلاَّهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ﴾.
The meaning is: he lowered them both into disobedience.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ﴾.
And this indicates that they did not go far in eating.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ﴾.
That is, they began to stick on [leaves]; and from it: خصفتُ النَّعْلَ, that is, I patched it.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was fig leaves; they took them and placed them over their private parts.
And the difference between the disobedience of Ādam and the disobedience of Iblīs is that Iblīs persisted in the sin, while Ādam repented and returned. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿قَالاَ رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أنْفُسَنَا وَإنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الخَاسِرِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَابَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاساً يُوَارِي سَوْءَاتِكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Some people of the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿يَابَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاساً يُوَارِي سَوْءَاتِكُمْ وَرِيشاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: الريشُ means wealth.
And al-Kisāʾī said: الريش means clothing.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: الريشُ and الرياشُ are the visible clothing and outward finery.
And الريشُ according to most lexicographers is whatever covers, whether clothing or livelihood.
And Sībawayh recited:
فَرِيشِي مِنْكُمُ وَهَوَايَ مَعْكُمْ * وَإِنْ كَانَتْ زِيَارَتُكُمْ لِمَامَا
(My provision is from you and my love is with you, even if your visits are but rare.)
And Abū Ḥātim related from Abū ʿUbayda: وهبتُ له دَابَّةً بريشها, that is: I gave him a mount with its covering and the trappings on it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: الرِّياشُ may be a plural of الرِّيش, and also of the same meaning, like لِبْس and لِبَاس.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾.
That is, the garment of piety is better than clothes, because the sinner, even if he wears clothes, is defiled.
And Qāsim ibn Mālik reported from ʿAwf from Maʿbadh al-Juhanī [Translator's note: the text reads «معْبَذٍ»; the well-known name is Maʿbad al-Juhanī, «معبد»], who said: ﴿لِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾ is modesty (al-ḥayāʾ).
And al-Aʿmash read: ﴿وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى خَيْرٌ﴾, and did not read ﴿ذلك﴾.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾.
قبيلُهُ: his troops.
Mujāhid said: He means the jinn and the devils.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا فَعَلُواْ فَاحِشَةً قَالُواْ وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَآ آبَاءَنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: The women used to circumambulate the House naked, wearing [only] the rihāṭ.
And he said: الرِّهاط is the plural of رَهْط, a strip of wool or of leather thongs; thus said al-Farrāʾ.
So this is the indecency (al-fāḥisha) about which they said ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَآ آبَاءَنَا﴾.
And someone else said: "The men used to circumambulate naked by day and the women by night, and they would say: We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we disobeyed Allah."

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّي بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
That is, justice.
﴿وَأَقِيمُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, face the qibla wherever you are, even if you are in a church.
And someone else said: Its meaning is: when the prayer comes upon you in a mosque, then pray, and let none of you say: I will pray only in my own mosque.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Whoever was begun as one of the blessed returns as one of the blessed, and whoever was begun as one of the wretched returns as one of the wretched.
And Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: A person's end is sealed with what he was begun with. Do you not see that the sorcerers were unbelievers, then their end was sealed with blessedness? And that Iblīs was with the angels as a believer, then returned to what he was begun with.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَابَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means clothing, because some people of the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked; and this is the position of Mujāhid.
And Shuʿba reported from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Muslim al-Baṭīn narrate from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "A woman would circumambulate the House naked, so ﴿خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾ was revealed."
Al-Zuhrī said: The Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except the Ḥums — Quraysh and their allies — so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said ﴿خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He, rebuking them: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَالْطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزْقِ﴾.
It is general.
And it is said: That is, who forbade wearing clothes in circumambulation? And who forbade what they forbade of the baḥīra and others?
Al-Farrāʾ said: Some tribes of the Arabs used not to eat meat during the days of their pilgrimage, and used to circumambulate naked, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, sent down this.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ هِي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا خَالِصَةً يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The Muslims and the polytheists share in it in this world, and it will be exclusively for the Muslims on the Day of Resurrection.
And it is said: ﴿فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ belongs to the ṣila (relative clause), that is: [for those who] believed at this time, [it being] pure of grief and vexation.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ ٱلْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ﴾.
Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda reported from Zakariyyā ibn Isḥāq, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا﴾: marrying [fathers' wives, called] mothers in the Jāhiliyya; ﴿وَمَا بَطَنَ﴾: fornication.
[Translator's note: the text reads «نكاحُ الأمهات», literally "marrying mothers"; the gloss in square brackets reflects the usual explanation, that stepmothers are meant.]
And Qatāda said: their secret and their open forms.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلإِثْمَ﴾.
And He said in another place: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الخَمْرِ وَالمَيْسِرِ، قُلْ فِيهما إثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾; so by these two verses He indicated that wine and gambling are forbidden.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ﴾.
That is, an appointed time.
﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً﴾.
The meaning is: they will not delay it by an hour nor by less than an hour; but the hour is singled out for mention because it is the smallest of the names of time spans.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: what wrongdoing is more hideous than fabricating against Allah and denying His signs?
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يَنَالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُم مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Jābir reported from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "What was decreed for them of good and evil."
And Sharīk reported from Sālim from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يَنَالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُم مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾; he said: of wretchedness and blessedness.
And Sufyān reported from Manṣūr from Mujāhid, who said: what they were promised in it of good and evil.
And the meaning of this view: that their share of the punishment reaches them according to the measure of their unbelief, like His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللهَ لاَ يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾
and ﴿إنَّ المُنَافِقِينَ فِى الدَّرْكِ الأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ﴾,
and He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَاباً صَعَداً﴾.
And likewise al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Its meaning is: their share of the punishment reaches them.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ﴾.
It is said: [They are] the helpers of the Angel of Death; when they came to them, they admitted that they had been unbelievers.
And it is said: the angels of punishment.
And the meaning of ﴿يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ﴾ on this view is: they cause them to die by punishment, as you say: I killed him with torment.
And it may be from taking the full count (istīfāʾ al-ʿadad).

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱدْخُلُواْ فِيۤ أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾.
It is said that the meaning of "في" is the meaning of "مع" (with). And this is not impossible, because your saying "زيدٌ في القوم" (Zayd is among the people) means: with the people. And it is possible for "في" to keep its basic meaning.
And al-Aṣmaʿī said concerning the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وَهَلْ يَنْعَمَنْ مَنْ كَانَ آخِرُ عَهْدِهِ * ثَلاَثِينَ شَهْراً فِي ثَلاَثَةِ أحْوَالِ
(Can one live at ease whose last acquaintance [with the abode] was thirty months, in three years?)
[that] the meaning of (في) is the meaning of (مع).
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا ٱدَّارَكُواْ فِيهَا﴾.
That is, they followed one upon another and gathered together.
﴿قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ لأُولاَهُمْ رَبَّنَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ أَضَلُّونَا﴾.
The meaning is: the last of them said: O our Lord, these led us astray; ﴿لأُولاَهُمْ﴾ means: concerning the first of them.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلَـٰكِن لاَّ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: but you do not know, O people of this world, the measure of the punishment they are in.
And it is possible that the meaning is: you do not know, O you who are addressed.
And whoever reads ﴿وَلَكِنْ لاَ يَعْلَمُون﴾, its meaning in his view is: but each party does not know the measure of the other party's punishment.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالَتْ أُولاَهُمْ لأُخْرَاهُمْ فَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, in lightening of the punishment.
And al-Suddī said: You went astray just as we went astray.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لاَ تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابُ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
It is said: He means the gates of Paradise, because Paradise is in heaven.
And the best of what has been said about this is what Sufyān reported from Manṣūr from Mujāhid, who said: "The gates of heaven will not be opened for their words nor for their deeds." And what indicates the soundness of this view is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ، والعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يرفَعُه﴾.
And on this there is a ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad), reported by al-Minhāl from Zādhān from al-Barāʾ from the Prophet ﷺ: "When the soul of the unbelieving or hypocritical servant departs, the angels take it until it reaches the lowest heaven, giving off the most putrid stench of a carcass that was ever on the face of the earth; then [the gate] is asked to be opened for him, but it is not opened." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿لاَ تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابُ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾. "Then Allah says: Place his record in Sijjīn and return him to the earth, and it is flung down." Then he, upon him be peace, recited: ﴿وَمَنْ
يُشْرِكْ باللهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَدْخُلُونَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ ٱلْخِيَاطِ﴾.
And the meaning is: they will never enter Paradise at all; and the Arabs use expressions like this a great deal.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was asked about the camel (al-jamal), and he said: It is the mate of the she-camel.
It was as though he considered ignorant the one who asked him about something all people know.
And it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلْجُمَّلُ﴾ with ḍamma on the jīm and doubling of the mīm, and said: It is the thick rope (al-qals) among the ropes of ships.
And Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: They are ropes gathered together, plural of جُمَّلة.
And it is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he read: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلْجُمَل﴾ with ḍamma on the jīm and the mīm undoubled.
It is said: It too is the thick rope.
And السَّمُّ and السُّمُّ: the eye of the needle; Ibn Sīrīn read it with ḍamma on the sīn.
And الخِيَاط and المِخْيَطُ: the needle; and its counterpart is قِنَاع and مِقْنَع.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.
He means the unbelievers, because mention of them has preceded.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَهُمْ مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ﴾.
That is, a bed.
﴿وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ﴾, that is, covering [upon covering] of punishment.
﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — it is said: He means the unbelievers. And Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ﴾.
الغِلُّ in the language is rancour. The meaning: none of them will bear rancour against another for what was between them in this world.
And it is possible that the meaning is: none of them will envy another for a higher rank.
And what indicates that the [right] view is the first is that it is reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's mercy be upon him, that he said: "I hope that I, ʿUthmān, Ṭalḥa and al-Zubayr will be among those of whom Allah said ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ﴾."
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَـٰذَا﴾.
That is, for what He brought us to of this.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنُودُوۤاْ أَن تِلْكُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: [they were called] with [the announcement] that this is the Garden.
And it is possible that "أنْ" is explicative (mufassira) of the call.
The Basrans gauge it by "أي" (that is), and the Kufans gauge it by "saying" (al-qawl); the meaning is the same. It is as though "ونُودُوا" [means]: it was said to them, This is the Garden; that is, this is that Garden which you were promised in the world.
And it is possible that when they saw it, it was said to them before they entered it: ﴿تِلْكُم ٱلْجَنَّة﴾.
And the account of the meaning of ﴿أنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا﴾ and ﴿أنْ لَعْنَةُ اللهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ follows what we said about ﴿أَن تِلْكُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ كُلاًّ بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: The people of Paradise are known by the whiteness of their faces, and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ﴾.
Most of the exegetes said: He means the people of the Heights (aṣḥāb al-aʿrāf).

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنَادَىٰ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَعْرَافِ رِجَالاً يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾.
Ḥudhayfa said: "The people of the Heights" are a people whose good deeds and evil deeds were equal, so they are between Paradise and the Fire; then Allah looked upon them and had mercy on them, and they said: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلاَ أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
And ʿUbaydallāh ibn Abī Yazīd reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: الأعرافُ is the elevated thing.
And Mujāhid reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: الأعراف is a wall that has a crest like the comb of a rooster.
And الأعراف in the language is the elevated place, plural of عُرْف.
And Abū Mijlaz said: They are among the angels.
He said: «والَّذِين صرفت أبصارهم تلقاء أصحاب النار» ("and those whose eyes are turned towards the people of the Fire") are the people of Paradise.
Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Dāwūd al-Ḍabbī narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Khālid narrated to us, saying: from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid concerning the people of the Heights; he said: They are a people whose good deeds and evil deeds were equal; they are on a wall between Paradise and the Fire, they are hoping to enter Paradise, and they will enter.
And it is said: The people of the Heights are angels between Paradise and the Fire.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is the better known and more familiar.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said to them: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلاَ أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: And they are called the poor folk of the people of Paradise.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَاهُمْ كَمَا نَسُواْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, We leave them in the Fire, just as they left [aside] the meeting of this Day of theirs.
And the meaning is: so today We leave them in the punishment, just as they left off working for the meeting of this Day of theirs.
﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ﴾, that is, for their denial of Our signs [Translator's note: مَا being maṣdariyya].

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ تَأْوِيلَهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, its recompense.
And Qatāda said: That is, its outcome.
And this is a good view, and its meaning is: what they were promised in it, that it will come to pass.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾.
He means the Day of Resurrection.
﴿يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they turned away from it.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي ٱلْلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ﴾.
The meaning is: He covers the day with the night and covers the night with the day; then [the second part] was omitted because the hearer knows it.
That is, He makes this enter into that, and that into this.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلاَ لَهُ ٱلْخَلْقُ وَٱلأَمْرُ﴾.
So He distinguished between the created thing and the command, which is His speech; this indicates that His speech is uncreated, and it is His saying "كُنْ" (Be).
And it is said: It is like His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّان﴾ [i.e. mentioning the particular after the general].
And it is said the meaning is: and the disposal of the command; then [the muḍāf] was omitted.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱدْعُواْ رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعاً﴾.
That is, humbly submissive and devoted in worship; ﴿وَخُفْيَةً﴾, that is, and keep worship hidden, because supplication is worship.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: This indicates that there is supplication that involves transgression; that is, do not transgress in supplication.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱدْعُوهُ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
And the meaning is: in fear of Him and in hope of what is with Him.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَاحَ نُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾.
نُشْرٌ is the plural of نَشُور; one says ريحٌ نَشُورٌ when it comes from here and there. And it is said: نُشُرٌ is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And whoever reads ﴿نُشْراً﴾ with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn — according to the Basrans he follows this meaning.
As for al-Farrāʾ, he claimed that it is a dialectal form in the sense of النَّشْر, as one says خَسْف and خُسْف.
And whoever reads ﴿نَشْراً﴾ holds that the meaning is: it spreads, a spreading (tanshuru nashran).
And whoever reads ﴿بُشْراً﴾, it is in his view the plural of بشير, lightened; it may be the plural of بُشرة, and it may be a maṣdar like العُمُر. And it is read ﴿بَشْراً﴾; and بُشراً is the maṣdar of بَشَرَه يَبْشُرهُ in the sense of بَشَّرَه (he gave him good tidings).
And the meaning of ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ is: ahead of the rain, which is from His mercy, the Exalted.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَقَلَّتْ سَحَاباً ثِقَالاً سُقْنَاهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ ٱلْمَآءَ﴾.
﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَقَلَّتْ سَحَاباً ثِقَالاً﴾, that is, until, when the wind carries clouds heavy with water, ﴿سُقْنَاهُ﴾ — meaning the clouds — ﴿لِبَلَدٍ مَّيِّتٍ فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ ٱلْمَآءَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: We sent down the water upon the land.
And it is possible that the meaning is: We sent down the water by means of the clouds; ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ مِن كُلِّ ¤لثَّمَرَاتِ﴾, that is, by means of the water.
And it is possible that the meaning is: in the land.
* And His saying the Exalted: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ ٱلْموْتَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Allah sends rain and it rains, and people sprout as crops sprout.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾.
That is, so that you may be in hope of taking admonition from what you are reminded of and told.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْبَلَدُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ وَٱلَّذِي خَبُثَ لاَ يَخْرُجُ إِلاَّ نَكِداً﴾.
النَّكِدُ in the language: the scant, the little. And this is a figurative representation (tamthīl).
Mujāhid said: He means that among the children of Ādam there are the good and the vile.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلْمَلأُ﴾.
The chiefs and the nobles, that is, those fully capable (al-maliʾūn) of what is entrusted to them.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَوْماً عَمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, [blind] to the truth.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلْمَلأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي سَفَاهَةٍ﴾.
السَّفَاهَةُ: thinness of forbearance, and rashness; one says ثوبٌ سفيهٌ (a flimsy garment) when it is light.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He, in reply to them: ﴿قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي سَفَاهَةٌ﴾.
And this is a lesson in good manners in bearing [insult] patiently.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحاً﴾.
It is said: He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said ﴿أَخَاهُمْ﴾ only because he was a human being like them, of the children of Ādam, whom they could understand, so it was a more binding proof against them.
And it is said: He said ﴿أخَاهُمْ﴾ only because he was of their clan.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ جَآءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ هَـٰذِهِ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً﴾.
It is narrated that she came out of a solid rock.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَبَوَّأَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, He settled you; and the poet said:
وَبُوِّئَتْ فِي صَمِيمِ مَعْشَرِهَا * فنمَّ فِي قَوْمِهَا مُبَوَّؤُهَا
(She was settled in the very heart of her clan, and her place of settling flourished among her people.)
And it is said: They used to hew houses out of the mountains only because of the length of their lives, since roofs and walls would collapse before their lives came to an end.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ آلآءَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: الآلاءُ are the favours.
And Abū ʿUbayda related: its singular is "ألَىً" and "إِلىً".
And someone else added: إلْيٌ.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَعَتَوْاْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
That is, they went to excess in unbelief.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ﴾.
الرَّجفة in the language is the violent earthquake.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَصْبَحُواْ فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾.
That is, fallen on their knees and their faces.
The origin of الجُثوم (crouching) is for hares and the like, and the place is مَجْثَم; the poet said:
بِهَا العِينُ وَالآرَامُ يَمْشِينَ خِلْفَةً * وَأطْلاَؤُهَا يَنْهَضْنَ مِنْ كُلِّ مَجْثَمِ
(In it the wide-eyed wild cows and the white gazelles walk in succession, and their young rise up from every crouching-place.)
And Maʿmar reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: When the Prophet ﷺ passed by al-Ḥijr, he said: "Do not ask for signs, for the people of Ṣāliḥ asked for them; she [the she-camel] used to come down to water through this mountain pass, but they defied the command of their Lord and hamstrung her, so the Shout seized them, and Allah stilled all of them who were under the sky, except one man who was in the sanctuary (ḥaram) of Allah; when he left the sanctuary, there befell him what had befallen his people."

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلُوطاً إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّن ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
By this He indicated that no one had preceded them in sodomy. And the meaning of ﴿إنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾ is: they keep themselves pure of the indecency.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَنجَيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلاَّ ٱمْرَأَتَهُ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَابِرِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: [Of] those who remained behind.
And الغابر according to the lexicographers is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād): غَابِرٌ is said of what remains, and غَابِرٌ is said of what has gone and passed away.
And it has been said concerning the verse that its meaning is ﴿مِنَ ٱلْغَابِرِينَ﴾ [i.e. left out] from salvation.
And it is said: of those who remained with the people of Lūṭ in the place where they were punished.
And Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: of those given long life, that is, she had become very old.
And Ḥudhayfa said: Jibrīl ﷺ lifted up their city, then overturned it; his [Lūṭ's] wife heard the crash, turned round, and was destroyed with them.
And most commonly in the language الغابر is the one remaining; the rajaz poet said:
فَمَا وَنَى مُحَمَّدٌ مُذْ أنْ غَفَرْ * لَهُ الإِلَهُ مَا مَضَى وَمَا غَبَرْ
(Muḥammad has not slackened since God forgave him what is past and what remains.)
that is: and what remains.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَبْخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ﴾.
البَخْسُ means diminishing.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ تُفْسِدُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلاَحِهَا﴾.
That is, after Allah had set it right by commanding justice and sending messengers.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, you threaten with harm whoever came to Shuʿayb and visited him and wanted Islam.
And one says: وعدتُه (I promised him) good or evil; but when you say وعدتُه [alone] it is only for good, and when you say أوعدتُه it is only for evil.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَتَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ وَتَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجاً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, and you seek the way to be crooked, away from the truth.
And السبيلُ is the road and the doctrine.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلاً فَكَثَّرَكُمْ﴾.
1- It is possible that they were few in number.
2- And it is possible that they were poor, and He multiplied them with wealth.
3- And it is possible that they were without power.
And Allah knows best what He intended; but in any case he reminded them of one of the favours of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, as He the Exalted said: ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا آلاَءَ اللهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلْمَلأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ مِن قَوْمِهِ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يٰشُعَيْبُ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَعَكَ مِن قَرْيَتِنَآ أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾.
It may be asked: How could they say this to Shuʿayb ﷺ when he was a prophet? There are two answers to this:
One of them: that the meaning of ﴿لَتَعُودُنَّ﴾ is "you will surely become", as you say: عاد عليَّ من فلان مكروهٌ (something hateful came [lit. returned] to me from so-and-so).
And the other answer: that since they included with him those of them who had believed, it was possible for them to say ﴿أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا﴾, meaning those who had believed.
﴿قَالَ أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كَارِهِينَ﴾? That is: shall we return to your religion even though we are unwilling? And his saying ﴿وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَا أنْ نَعُودَ فِيهَا إلاَّ أنْ يَشَاءَ اللهُ رَبُّنَا﴾ is by way of submission to Allah, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا تَوْفِيقِي إلاَّ باللهِ﴾.
And the proof of this is that after it comes ﴿وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً، عَلَى اللهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا، رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالحَقِّ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, judge between us and our people with the truth.
And Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid reported from Abū Ṣāliḥ concerning His saying the Exalted ﴿افْتَحْ بَينِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحاً﴾; he said: Its meaning is victory.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ فِيهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, as though they had not lived and enjoyed comfort.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: One says غَنِينَا بمكان كذا, that is, we resided in such-and-such a place; and dwellings are called المغاني.
And the meaning of ﴿فَكَيْفَ آسَى﴾? is: so how should I grieve? And الأسى is the most intense grief.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّبِيٍّ إِلاَّ أَخَذْنَا أَهْلَهَا بِٱلْبَأْسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ﴾.
Murra said, from Ibn Masʿūd: البأساءُ is poverty, and الضَرَّاءُ is illness.
And it is said: البأساءُ is calamities in wealth; one says بَئِسَ الرَّجُلُ يَبْأَسُ بَأْساً وبَأْسَاء when he becomes poor.
And الضَرَّاءُ is what befalls of illnesses and calamities in the body.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَضَّرَّعُونَ﴾, that is, they humble themselves and submit.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ ٱلسَّيِّئَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The evil (al-sayyiʾa) is hardship, and the good (al-ḥasana) is ease and children.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ عَفَوْاْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, their wealth and children increased.
And this is well known in the language; and from it is the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "أعْفُوا اللِّحى", that is, let the beards grow abundant.
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, reported of them that they did not take a lesson from what befell them, and said: The norm of time is good and evil; so He the Exalted said: ﴿وَّقَالُواْ قَدْ مَسَّ آبَاءَنَا ٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَٱلسَّرَّآءُ فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بَغْتَةً﴾.
That is, suddenly.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ آمَنُواْ وَٱتَّقَواْ﴾.
A city is called قرية because people gather in it, from قريتُ الماءَ (I collected the water) when you gather it.
And the blessings that come from the sky are rain, and those that come from the earth are vegetation.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَفَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتاً وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ﴾.
That is: do those who deny Muḥammad ﷺ feel secure that Our might will come upon them ﴿بَيَاتاً﴾, that is, by night?

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا ضُحًى وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾.
And the meaning of ﴿وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ is: while they are engaged in what does not benefit them.
Anyone engaged in what harms him and does not benefit him is called لاَعِب (one who plays).

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَفَأَمِنُواْ مَكْرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, His punishment when it falls upon them while they do not know that it is falling upon them.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, has it not been made clear? And the meaning of ﴿يَهْدِ﴾ with the yāʾ: it becomes plain and clear.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: This is like His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعَادُوا لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾.
And someone else said: This is specific to particular peoples, of whom Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, reported that they would not believe.
As for the view of whoever said that the meaning of ﴿فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ is "so that faith be judged for them", it is not sound in the language; and what shows its falsity is that after it comes ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, which indicates that their hearts had been sealed. This is the view of Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] — as a requital for what they did.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لأَكْثَرِهِم مِّنْ عَهْدٍ﴾
"مِنْ" is redundant (zāʾida), and it indicates the meaning of the genus; were it not for "مِنْ", it might be imagined that it is a single one in meaning.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning is: We found in most of them neither keeping [of covenant] nor fidelity.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَا فَٱنْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾
The basic meaning of ẓulm (wrongdoing) is putting a thing in other than its proper place; so when they disbelieved in them [the signs], they put unbelief in the place of the faith that was due; hence it was said ﴿ظَلَمُواْ بِهَا﴾ in the sense of: they disbelieved in them.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لاَّ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, eager.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is [also] the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: ﴿حَقِيقٌ أنْ لاَ أقُولَ﴾; and this points to the lightened form [Translator's note: i.e. without the preposition], because prepositions are elided with "أنْ".
And al-Kisāʾī said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: ﴿حقيقٌ بأنْ لاَ أقُولَ عَلَى اللهِ إلاَّ الحقَّ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning of ﴿عَلَى أَنْ لاَّ﴾ and ﴿بأنْ لاَ﴾ is one, as one says: جاء فلانٌ على حالٍ حَسَنَةٍ and بحالٍ حسنة (so-and-so came in a good state).
And whoever reads ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلَيَّ أنْ لاَ أقُولَ عَلَى اللهِ إلاَّ الحقَّ﴾, its meaning in his view is: it is incumbent upon me.

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾
الثعبانُ is the male serpent. And the meaning of ﴿وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ﴾ is: he displayed it.
Mujāhid said: He brought it out from the opening of his garment, white without leprosy.
And it is narrated that Mūsā ﷺ was dark-skinned, so when he brought out his hand white, that was a sign.

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلْمَلأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾
الملأ according to most lexicographers means the nobles; and in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: O Muḥammad, do you know about what the Highest Assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā) dispute?"
And some lexicographers said: الملأُ is the group (al-rahṭ), and النَّفَرُ is men with no women among them.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾
Qatāda said: That is, detain him.
And what is well known among the lexicographers is that one says أرجَأْتُ الأمْرَ when you postpone the matter.
And whoever reads ﴿أرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾ — there are two views on his reading:
The sounder of them is that it is a dialectal form, even if it is not widely known.
And the other view: it is related from Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad]; he said: It is from رَجَا يَرْجُو, that is, leave him hoping.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ﴾
That is, they sought to arouse fear in them.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ﴾
And the meaning of ﴿تَلْقَفُ﴾ is: it swallows up.
Abū Ḥātim said: It reached me that in some readings it is ﴿تَلَقَّمُ﴾ with mīm and doubling.
And Khārija said: Al-Ḥasan read ﴿تَلْقَمُ﴾ with fatḥa on the qāf.
Mujāhid said: The meaning of ﴿مَا يَأْفِكُونَ﴾ is: what they lie [with], that is, by means of it; and their lie was that they made the ropes [appear as] snakes.
And it is possible that ﴿فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾? is an answer from Pharaoh to the chiefs when they said: ﴿إنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ. يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكُمَ مِنْ أرْضِكُمْ﴾, so Pharaoh said ﴿فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾?
And it is possible that the chiefs said this to Pharaoh and those close to him.
Mujāhid said: The meaning of ﴿فَوَقَعَ الحَقُّ﴾ is: it became manifest.
And the meaning of ﴿أفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْراً﴾ is: send down upon us patience that envelops us.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَذَرَكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ﴾
Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿إلاَهَتَكَ﴾ and said: Its meaning is: and your worship [i.e. the worship of you], because Pharaoh was worshipped and did not worship.
And the one who argued for this reading said: The proof that he was worshipped and did not worship is that he said: ﴿مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْ إلَهٍ غَيْرِي﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿وَآلِهَتَكَ﴾ takes one of two directions:
One of them: that by the gods here he means those whom Pharaoh obeyed, as was said concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أرْبَاباً مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ﴾ — that they did not worship them but obeyed them, so it became a figurative representation.
And the other direction: that Sulaymān al-Taymī said: It reached me that Pharaoh used to worship cattle.
Al-Taymī said: So I said to al-Ḥasan: Did Pharaoh worship anything? He said: Yes, he used to worship something that Allah had placed on his neck.
And Ismāʿīl said: Pharaoh's saying ﴿أنَا رَبُّكُمُ الأَعْلَى﴾ indicates that they used to worship something other than him.
And the meaning of ﴿وَآلِهَتَكَ﴾ may be that they were gods which he commanded them to worship.

nahhas-meani:129-129.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أُوذِينَا مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَأْتِينَا وَمِن بَعْدِ مَا جِئْتَنَا﴾
Mujāhid said: That is, before you were sent to us.
And someone else said: The harm that befell them before he was sent to them was the killing of their sons; and the harm that befell them afterwards was that Pharaoh said: ﴿سَنُقَتِّلُ أبْنَاءَهُمْ، وَنَسْتَحْيِي نِسَاءَهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:130-130.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَآ آلَ فِرْعَونَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ﴾
Mujāhid said: That is, with blights.
And it is well known in the language to say: أصابتهم سَنَةٌ, that is, drought. Its implied form (taqdīr) is سَنَةُ جَدْبٍ (a year of drought), then [the muḍāf ilayhi] was omitted.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنَقْصٍ مِّن ٱلثَّمَرَاتِ﴾
Mujāhid said: That is, less than that.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾
That is, take a lesson from what befell them.

nahhas-meani:131-131.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَـٰذِهِ﴾
Mujāhid said: The good here is well-being and ease. ﴿لَنَا هَـٰذِهِ﴾, that is: it has come to us by right.
And someone other than Mujāhid said: That is, it is the norm that good befalls us.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The evil here is affliction; and the meaning of ﴿يَطَّيَّرُواْ﴾ is: they regard as an ill omen.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّمَا طَائِرُهُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّمَا طَائِرُهُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, the ill fortune lies only in what will befall them on the Day of Resurrection of the evil they were promised.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
That is, they are heedless of this.

nahhas-meani:133-133.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ﴾
ʿAṭāʾ said: الطوفانُ is death.
And Mujāhid said: It is death in every form.
And Qatāda said: The water flowed over them until they stood upright [in it], so they asked Mūsā to pray to Allah to remove it, and he did.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: A great quantity of rain came upon them, so they asked Mūsā to pray to Allah to remove it from them, and they would send the Children of Israel with him. So he prayed to Allah, and He removed it from them, and the land became verdant and fertile; but they went back [on their word] and did not send the Children of Israel with him. So Allah poured the locusts upon their crops and they ate them; then they asked Mūsā, and he prayed to Allah and He removed that from them; then they went back again.
Abū Jaʿfar said: الطُّوفانُ in the language is whatever is destructive, whether death or flood, that is, whatever encompasses them and destroys them.
Mujāhid said: Allah sent the locusts upon them, and they ate the nails of their doors and their clothes; and He sent upon them the qummal — which is the wingless young locust (al-dabā) — and it would get into their clothes and their bedding.
And ʿIkrima said: القُمَّل are the grasshoppers (al-janādib), the offspring of locusts.
And Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said: القُمَّلُ are the dung beetles (al-juʿlān).
And القُمَّلُ according to the lexicographers is a kind of tick.
Abū al-Ḥasan al-Aʿrābī al-ʿAdawī said: القُمَّلُ are small creatures of the tick family, except that they are smaller than it; its singular is قُمَّلَة.
And this does not contradict what the exegetes said, because it is possible that all these things were sent upon them, and they all have in common that they harm them.
Mujāhid said: They would find blood in their clothes, their drink and their food. And the meaning of ﴿آيَاتٍ مّفَصَّلاَتٍ﴾ is: separated from one another, with a period of time between each one of them.
It is narrated that between one sign and the next there were eight days.

nahhas-meani:134-134.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلرِّجْزُ﴾
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read: ﴿الرُّجْز﴾.
Mujāhid said: And it is the punishment.
﴿قَالُواْ يٰمُوسَىٰ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: By what He enjoined upon you and made known to you.
﴿لَئِن كَشَفْتَ عَنَّا ٱلرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَآئِيلَ﴾ — it is narrated that they had been overworking them.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إلَى أجَلٍ هُمْ بَالِغُوهُ﴾: until a named number, [namely] their days.
﴿فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ فِي اليَمِّ﴾, and it is the sea.

nahhas-meani:137-137.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشَارِقَ ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا ٱلَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾
The people here are the Children of Israel, and among them were "Dāwūd" and "Sulaymān", peace be upon them both.
Qatāda said: The [land] that was blessed is Syria (al-Shām).
And it is said: Egypt.
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَآئِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ﴾
It is said: By the word He means: ﴿عَسَى رَبَّكُمْ أنْ يُهْلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفَكُمْ فِي الأرْضِ﴾
Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْرِشُونَ﴾:
he said: They build houses and dwellings.
And the meaning of ﴿يَعْكُفُونَ﴾ is: they persist and keep constantly to [something]; and from it is said: اعتكفَ فلانٌ (so-and-so went into retreat).
And the meaning of ﴿مُتَبَّرٌ﴾ is: destroyed and ruined; one says تَبَّرْتُ الشَّيءَ when you have broken the thing, and the name of what is broken off from it is التِّبْر.

nahhas-meani:140-140.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ إِلَـٰهاً﴾
The meaning of أبغي is: I seek. And the meaning of ﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾ is: they inflict on you.

nahhas-meani:141-141.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَفِي ذٰلِكُمْ بَلاۤءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ﴾
It is possible that the meaning is: and in His delivering the Children of Israel there is a favour.
And it is possible that the meaning is: in your inflicting [Translator's note: the text reads «في سومكم بني إسرائيل», literally "in your inflicting on the Children of Israel"; the intended sense is presumably Pharaoh's people inflicting it on them] on the Children of Israel the worst of torment there is a great trial.

nahhas-meani:142-142.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَوَاعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلاَثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْنَاهَا بِعَشْرٍ﴾
Mujāhid said: The thirty are Dhū al-Qaʿda, and the ten are ten of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
And the benefit of His saying ﴿فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ is that it indicated that the ten were nights and not hours.
And it is said: It is for emphasis (tawkīd).
And it is said: It is equivalent to "so that is [the total]", that is, there is nothing after it worth mentioning.

nahhas-meani:143-143.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَاتِنَا﴾
That is, for the appointed time which We appointed for him.
﴿وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾, that is, He singled him out for that.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكّاً﴾
Qatāda said: Part of it crushed another part.
And ʿIkrima said: It is only ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكَّاءَ﴾, from الدَّكَّاوات (low mounds); and the implied construction (taqdīr) on this reading is: He made it a دكَّاء land, which is the slightly raised [ground] that does not reach the size of a mountain.
ʿIkrima said: When Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, looked at the mountain, it became a desert of dust.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَخَرَّ موسَىٰ صَعِقاً﴾
It is said: dead.
And Saʿīd ibn ʿArūba [Translator's note: so in the text; the well-known transmitter from Qatāda is Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba] said, from Qatāda: swooning; ﴿فَلَمَّا أفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ إنِّي تُبْتُ إلَيْكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, I repent of asking You for the vision; ﴿وَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is, the first to believe that no one sees You in this world without dying, because his request was [to see Him] in this world.
Qatāda said: When he took the Tablets and saw in them the description of the community of Muḥammad ﷺ and their praise, he said: O Lord, make them my community. He said: That is the community of Aḥmad. He said: Then make me one of them. He said: You will not live to meet them. And He said: O Mūsā, ﴿إنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالاَتِي وَبِكَلاَمِي﴾; so Mūsā ﷺ was content.

nahhas-meani:145-145.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي ٱلأَلْوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾
Sufyān said: That is, of the lawful and the unlawful.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مَّوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلاً لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, a detailed explanation of what they were commanded and forbidden.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَخُذْهَا بِقُوَّةٍ﴾
That is, with strength in your religion and your argument; and it is said: with earnestness and resolve.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُواْ بِأَحْسَنِهَا﴾
But all of it is good?
It is said: The meaning is that they were commanded to adopt what is better among what is permitted to them, even though both are permitted, like His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلَمَنِ انْتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُوْلَئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ﴾ — this is permissible, but pardon is better.
And it is said: ﴿بِأَحْسَنِهَا﴾ means by what is good in it.
And it is said: They were commanded something and told what [reward] they would have in it, and forbidden something and told what [penalty] they would bear in it; so it was said to them: adopt the best of it.
