And it is said: [It means] the abrogating [ruling].
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿سَأُوْرِيكُمْ دَارَ ٱلْفَاسِقِينَ﴾
Al-Ḥasan said: He means Hell.
And Mujāhid said: He means their destination in the Hereafter.
And Qasāma ibn Zuhayr read: ﴿سَأُورِثُكُمْ دَارَ الفَاسِقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:146-146.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آيَاتِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾
Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said: That is, I will keep them from [understanding] My Book.
Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: I will make their requital for their unbelief being led astray from the guidance of My signs.
And it is said: I will turn them away from benefiting from them.
And it is said: from their glory.
And the meaning of ﴿يَتَكَبَّرُونَ﴾: they despise people and consider themselves superior to them, and they are too proud to believe and follow the Prophet ﷺ.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِن يَرَوْاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلْغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلاً﴾
And it is read: ﴿سَبيلَ الرَّشَدِ﴾.
And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ read ﴿سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: الرُّشْدُ is soundness [in worldly affairs], and الرَّشَدُ is in religion.
Someone else said: الغيُّ is error.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنْهَا غَافِلِينَ﴾
It is possible that in their abandoning faith and reflection on the truth they are like the heedless.
And it is possible that they are heedless of what they will be requited with, as one says: How heedless so-and-so is of what is intended for him!

nahhas-meani:148-148.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَىٰ مِن بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلاً جَسَداً لَّهُ خُوَارٌ﴾.
That is, after he had come to the appointed time.
﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾ — fine things of gold and silver are called حَلْيٌ, and the plural is حُلِيٌّ and حِلِيٌّ. ﴿عِجْلاً جَسَداً﴾, that is, a calf as a [mere] body, that is, it had no reason or discernment.
And it is said: It had no head; it was only a body. ﴿لَّهُ خُوَارٌ﴾, that is, a sound [lowing].
Mujāhid said: He gathered the ornaments, then took a handful from the hoofprint of the horse of Jibrīl ﷺ and threw it onto it.

nahhas-meani:149-149.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِيۤ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَرَأَوْاْ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّواْ﴾.
Of one who is remorseful and bewildered it is said: سُقِطَ في يديه and أُسْقِطَ.
And it is read: ﴿وَلَمَّا سَقَطَ فِيۤ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is, when remorse fell into their hands.

nahhas-meani:150-150.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفاً﴾.
الأَسِفُ: intensely angry, enraged; and it can mean grief-stricken.
And the meaning of ﴿أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾? is: did you rush ahead and not wait for His command and His prohibition?
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَلْقَى ٱلأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They [the Tablets] were of green emerald.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: He means those who worshipped the calf.

nahhas-meani:151-151.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِي وَلأَخِي﴾.
That is, forgive the anger for which I threw down the Tablets, and forgive my brother his leniency towards the Children of Israel, since that was out of fear of Mūsā's anger, when he said: ﴿إنِّي خَشِيتُ أنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إسْرَائِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي﴾.
And it is said: He sought forgiveness only for sins that were before this time, because his anger too was for Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; and Hārūn, peace be upon him, only held back [from confronting] the Children of Israel so that they would not split up and fight one another.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Nothing remained of the Tablets except a sixth of them."

nahhas-meani:152-152.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ ٱلْعِجْلَ سَيَنَالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ﴾.
The meaning is: those who took the calf as a god; [the second object] was omitted because the hearer knows it.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿وَذِلَّةٌ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ is that it is the jizya (poll tax).
And it is said: It is what they were commanded, that they kill one another, and what they saw of their own going astray; Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَرَأَوْا أنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّوا﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this view is sounder than the first, because the jizya is taken from them [Translator's note: so in the text; the argument requires "is not taken from them", i.e. «لا تؤخذ منهم»]; it was only taken from their descendants.

nahhas-meani:154-154.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَماَّ سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلْغَضَبُ﴾.
Its meaning is: subsided.
Abū Isḥāq said: One says سَكَتَ، يَسْكُت، سَكْتاً when it subsides; and سَكَتَ، يَسْكُتُ، سُكُوتاً وَسَكْتاً when one stops speaking.
And the meaning of ﴿وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا﴾ is: and in what was copied from them, that is, in them is guidance and mercy.
Ibn Kaysān said: ﴿وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا﴾ — there are two views on it:
One of them: that they were renewed for him on two tablets.
And it is said: in what was copied from them; they had broken and most of them were lost, and what could be was copied from them; and in that copy is ﴿هُدَىً﴾, that is, clarification, ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾, that is, what points to that which brings about mercy. Hence He said: ﴿هُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning of the (اللاَّم) is the meaning of (من أجل), "for the sake of", as you say: أنا أكْرِمُ فلاناً لَكَ (I honour so-and-so for your sake).
And it is possible that the meaning is: their fear [is] of their Lord.

nahhas-meani:155-155.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلاً لِّمِيقَاتِنَا﴾.
That is, of those who had not worshipped the calf; and the meaning is: from his people [Translator's note: the preposition being omitted].
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They were made to die, then brought back to life.
And الرَّجْفةُ in the language is the violent earthquake; and it is narrated that they were shaken until they died.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The quake seized them only because they did not forbid those who worshipped the calf, though they did not approve of its worship.
﴿قَالَ رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ وَإِيَّايَ﴾, that is, You would have caused them to die, as He the Exalted said: ﴿إنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ﴾.
Ibn Kaysān said: That is, had You willed, ﴿أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ﴾, because they sinned in not forbidding those who worshipped the calf;
﴿وَإِيَّايَ﴾ for my sin when I killed the Copt. Yet You had mercy on us and did not destroy us for our own sins; would You then destroy us for the sins of the foolish who worshipped the calf, when You have favoured us with pardon before this?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The real meaning is: You will not destroy us; and the alif of interrogation indicates this meaning in many places, as you say: ما أنا أفعَلُ مثلَ هذا, that is, I do not do it.
﴿إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا﴾, that is, by the trial, ﴿مَن تَشَآءُ﴾ to test, and so make him disobedient.

nahhas-meani:156-156.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱكْتُبْ لَنَا فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدْنَـآ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya and Qatāda said concerning His saying the Exalted ﴿إِنَّا هُدْنَـآ إِلَيْكَ﴾: they said: We have repented.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿عَذَابِيۤ أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشَآءُ وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: It encompasses the righteous and the wicked in this world, and it is exclusively for the God-fearing on the Day of Resurrection.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَـاةَ﴾.
Ḥammād ibn Salama reported from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, ordained it for this community.

nahhas-meani:157-157.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلأُمِّيَّ﴾.
الأميُّ: the one who does not write.
And it is said: The Prophet ﷺ is attributed to Umm al-Qurā, which is Mecca.
﴿ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوباً عِندَهُمْ فِي ٱلتَّوْرَاةِ وَٱلإِنْجِيلِ﴾ — this was one of his proofs ﷺ, because he informed them of what was in their scripture.
So it is possible that ﴿يَأْمُرُهُم بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمُنْكَرِ﴾ is part of what is written with them.
And it is possible that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
﴿وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾.
It may be the lawful.
And it may be what had been forbidden to them of food.
﴿وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْخَبَآئِثَ﴾ — the Arabs call everything unlawful خَبِيثٌ (foul).
﴿وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: الإصْرُ is severity of worship.
And two views on it are reported from Mujāhid:
Ibn Abī Najīḥ reported from him that he said: Things had been made severe for them, so whoever embraced Islam and believed in the Prophet ﷺ had it lightened for him.
And Mūsā ibn Qays reported from him that he said: They are covenants that were binding on them.
And the two views are close, that is: what was heavy upon them.
And likewise the shackles (al-aghlāl) that were upon them — it is only a figurative representation (tamthīl), that is, things they had been charged with and made responsible for [Translator's note: the text reads «كُلِّفُوعا», evidently a misprint for «كُلِّفُوها»], so they are like shackles.
And it is narrated that if urine got on the skin of one of them, he was obliged to cut it off; and if a man killed a man, there was no avoiding killing him, and no blood-money (diya) was accepted from him.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ﴾.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿وَعَزَّرُوهُ﴾ is: and they honoured him.
And it is said: and they defended him from his enemies; and the meanings are close.
﴿ٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾ — like light in [its] clarity.
Then He said: ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللهِ وَرَسُولِهِ النَّبِيِّ الأُمِّيِّ الَّذِي يُؤْمِنُ بِالله وَكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The meaning of ﴿يُؤْمِنُ باللهِ وَكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾ is: he believes in Allah and in ʿĪsā.
And someone else said: The word (al-kalima) and speech (al-kalām) are the same here.

nahhas-meani:160-160.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُ ٱثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطاً أُمَماً﴾.
الأسباطُ are the divisions, and the singular is سِبْط; the asbāṭ among the descendants of Isḥāq ﷺ are like the tribes among the descendants of Ismāʿīl ﷺ.
And الأسباطُ is taken from السَّبَط, which is a plant on which camels are fed.
And the meaning of ﴿فَٱنبَجَسَتْ﴾ is: it gushed forth.

nahhas-meani:163-163.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَسْئَلْهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ ٱلْبَحْرِ﴾.
He commanded him to ask them a question of rebuke, to make them admit what they knew of their forefathers' disobedience, and to inform them of what cannot be known except from a scripture or revelation.
Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, saying: Yūnus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us — and likewise Ḥaywa informed me — from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: The town that was by the sea is Tiberias; and the town concerning which He said ﴿وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلاً أصْحَابَ القَرْيَةِ﴾ is Antioch.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱلَّتِي كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ ٱلْبَحْرِ﴾ is Ayla.
And the meaning of ﴿يَعْدُونَ﴾ is: they transgress and overstep the truth.
And الشُّرَّعُ means visible [at the surface].
And al-Ḥasan read ﴿يُسْبِتُون﴾, that is, they enter upon the Sabbath,
like "أهْلَلْنَا" (we entered upon the new month). And whoever reads with fatḥa on the bāʾ said its meaning is: they venerate the Sabbath,
as they used to venerate it. This is the view of al-Kalbī and Abū ʿUbayda.
Mujāhid said: The fish used to come to them on the Sabbath without their seeking them, as a trial from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, for them, that is, a test.

nahhas-meani:164-164.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا قَالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِّنْهُمْ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْماً ٱللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَاباً شَدِيداً﴾.
The meaning of (أو) here is [the occurrence of] one of the two things; that is, there has appeared from them that on account of which one of these two will befall them.
﴿قَالُواْ مَعْذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: our admonition is an excuse; that is, it is only incumbent on us to enjoin what is right upon them, and perhaps they will turn back through our admonition.
﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ﴾, that is, they abandoned [it], ﴿أنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوْءِ، وأخَذْنَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I do not know what was done with the group that neither enjoined nor forbade.
And someone else said: It was saved, because it did not take part like those who disobeyed.
Mujāhid said: ﴿بَئيس﴾ means painful, severe; and this is well known in the language: one says بَؤُسَ, so it is يبأسُ, when it becomes severe.
And whoever reads ﴿بِيسٍ﴾ — there are two views on it:
Al-Kisāʾī said: The origin of it is "بَئِسٌ"; the hamza was lightened, so two yāʾs met, one of them was elided, and its first letter was given kasra, as one says رَغِيف and شَهِيد [with initial kasra in dialect].
And it is said: He intended بَئِس on the pattern فَعِل; its first letter was given kasra, the hamza was lightened and the kasra [of the hamza] was dropped, as one says رَحِمٌ and رَحْمٌ.
Abū Isḥāq said: بئيسٍ means severe; and بَئِسَ [is said] when one becomes poor, and بَؤُسَ when it becomes severe.
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: بِيْسٌ means bad, and it does not follow the pattern of the verb; it is rather as one says ناقةٌ نِضْوٌ (an emaciated she-camel). And the Arabs say: "جاء ببناتٍ بِيسٍ", that is, he brought something bad.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are other readings of it besides these two; we will mention them in the Iʿrāb [Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān], if Allah wills.

nahhas-meani:167-167.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكَ لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ مَن يَسُومُهُمْ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾.
The exegetes said: Its meaning is: your Lord made known.
And this is a good view, because تعلَّم is said in the sense of "know!" [Translator's note: lit. أعْلَمَ, the pattern تفعَّل being used in the sense of the simple form]; and Abū Isḥāq recited from Zuhayr on the like of this:
فقلتُ تَعَلَّمْ إنَّ للصَّيْدِ غِرَّةً * فَإنْ لاَ تُضَيِّعْهَا فَإنَّكَ قَاتِلُهْ
(So I said: Know that the game has a moment off guard; if you do not waste it, you will kill it.)
And it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ مَن يَسُومُهُمْ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾: he said: He means the taking of the jizya.
If it is said: But they were transformed [into apes], so how could the jizya be taken from them?
The answer: It is taken from their sons; they were transformed, and humiliation attached to their children, so they are the most humiliated of peoples, and they are the Jews.
Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salāma narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā ibn Isḥāq al-Anṣārī narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ḥimmānī narrated to us, from Yaʿqūb al-Qummī, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكَ لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾: he said: the Arabs; ﴿مَن يَسُومُهُمْ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾: he said: the land tax (al-kharāj).
And it is said: "عَلَيْهِمْ" means upon the Jews; He made clear that He had foretold that.

nahhas-meani:168-168.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أُمَماً﴾.
That is, We divided them into groups.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَبَلَوْنَاهُمْ بِٱلْحَسَنَاتِ وَٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾.
That is, and We tested them with hardship and ease, with fertility and drought.

nahhas-meani:169-169.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ وَرِثُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Christians.
And someone else said: He means their sons.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is the more fitting of the two views — and Allah knows best — because a man's offspring is called his خَلْف; it is said of one, of two, of a plural and of the feminine in a single form, and the plural is خُلُوف.
And it is said: It is used only for the bad among the sons.
As for الخَلَف with a vowel on the lām, it is the replacement for a thing, whether offspring or other.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَـٰذَا ٱلأَدْنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They go after this world and consume it, and they give [self-serving] interpretations of the Book of Allah; this is the meaning of His saying the Exalted ﴿وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِّثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They take whatever there is in their day, lawful or unlawful, and if they find the same for the morrow, they take it.
And someone else said: They take bribes in judgement and say: We will be forgiven — and they do not repent.
And what indicates that they do not repent is His saying the Exalted ﴿وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِّثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾.
And العرض (ʿaraḍ) in the language is all the goods of this world.
And العَرْض with sukūn on the rāʾ is whatever wealth there is other than dīnārs and dirhams; and what is of dīnārs and dirhams is called نقد (cash), and so on.
And the meaning of ﴿وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِ﴾ is: they have read it, and they are recent in their reading of it.
